scope: Local implementation and focused regression review of experimental strict expanded reranking; no native build, operation, or performance run was performed for this fix by this agent.

behavior.default: SingleHopFilterSearch::new and SearchMode::single_hop_filter retain expanded candidates for exact reranking.
behavior.ablation: SingleHopFilterSearch::with_frontier_reranking and SearchMode::single_hop_filter_frontier preserve the original final-PQ-frontier policy.
behavior.established_modes: Graph, InlineFilter, MultihopFilter, FlatScan and DiverseGraph postprocessing defaults are unchanged.
behavior.pre_pq_filter: expand_beam_accept_only is unchanged; rejected neighbor IDs do not reach PQ/vector distance evaluation.
behavior.traversal_state: The strict traversal priority queue is fixed at exactly L. Matching dataset entry points consume ordinary frontier slots rather than adding frozen-point slots. Expanded candidate records are O(hops), unique under visited deduplication, and do not widen traversal. The disk exact-distance cache already retains O(hops) entries.
behavior.disk_io: Expanded reranking accepts only IDs already present in the exact-distance cache; it performs no uncached rerank loads, including when the I/O budget truncates a selected beam.

before_fix.failure: assert exact winner ID 0; actual frontier-only winner ID 4

regression.causal_claim: With no PQ or exact-distance ties and identical traversal, retaining expanded candidates recovers an exact winner evicted from the bounded PQ frontier. This proves the mechanism, not its numerical contribution to any benchmark label.

clippy.scope: Full two-crate all-target check passed for the expanded-reranking change before the exact-L and separate lifecycle-module integration. The exact-L core was subsequently rechecked by the dedicated core all-target command below. The native lifecycle integration is independently in progress and must clear temporary dead-code warnings before its final whole-crate clippy.

validation.note: A dependency reports a future-incompatibility notice for proc-macro-error2; no denied warnings or test failures remain in the listed successful checks. Transient builder-module compilation failures during another agent's edits were retried after that owner corrected them.

separate_unmodified_differences.evidence: C++ include/neighbor.h:25-28 orders by (distance, ID); Rust neighbor/queue.rs:142-168 and get_lower_bound:229 onward insert by distance alone. Ties can change boundary membership and traversal.

C++ uses the same (distance, ID) comparator to sort full_retset. Rust disk_provider.rs:536 uses fast_distance with sort_unstable_by. Equal-distance results can differ in strict-ID recall without different distance quality.

C++ selects the closest PQ-scored label medoid, pq_flash_index.cpp:1383-1396; Rust accepts all supplied matching starts. Existing benchmark artifacts have one entry point per label, so this is not a difference for those artifacts.

cpp_comparison.performance_and_per_label_attribution: Root is coordinating native expanded/frontier ablation; no native results are included in this local evidence. The test proves a candidate-loss mechanism and a queue-capacity difference without quantifying aggregate native performance.
cpp_comparison.resolved_capacity_difference: Both strict policies now use exactly L, matching C++ retset.reserve(l_search); other Rust graph modes retain their existing L + frozen/start behavior.

prior_native_evidence.note: Existing frozen native results, rust-final-review.json and final-native-inventory.json describe the earlier frontier-only prototype and must not be presented as measurements of this change.

capacity_regression.scope: Exact L applies to expanded and frontier strict policies only; established modes unchanged.
